source_text: ὧν πάντων ὁ ὑπερφρονῶν ὑπερκόσμιος ἔσται ποιῶν 49 τὰ θελήματα τοῦ θεοῦ τῷ μένειν ἀεὶ καὶ ἀγαπᾶν τὸν θεόν. (Cr 116, 16-23 Ma 218) Τοῦτό φησιν, ἐπειδὴ γεγονότες μαθηταὶ ἀπέστησαν μὲν τῆς ἀληθείας, ἰδίας δὲ ἐπινοίας βλασφημιῶν ἐξεῦρον. (Cr 118, 27-28) 50 Ὁ διειληφὼς ἐπιστημονικῶς περὶ θεοῦ ὡς ὄντος κατ' οὐσίαν δικαίου εὐθέως γνῶσιν ἕξει, ὡς γεννᾶται ἐκ τούτου ὁ τὴν δικαιοσύνην αὐτοῦ ποιῶν· ὥσπερ ὁ γνοὺς αὐτὸν ἁγιασμὸν ὄντα ἐπιδίδωσιν ἑαυτὸν τῷ ἁγιασθῆναι ἐπιστάμενος 51 ἀκριβῶς τό· “ἅγιοι ἔσεσθε, ὅτι ἐγὼ ἅγιός εἰμι”· εὖ δὲ καὶ τὸ φάναι “ποιῶν”, ἀλλ' οὐ ποιήσας ἢ ποιήσων δικαιοσύνην· δίκαιον παρίστησιν ἡ ἀρετὴ τὸν ἐνεργοῦντα πρακτικὴ οὖσα· οὐδεὶς οὖν πρὸ ποιήσεως αὐτῆς δίκαιός ἐστιν οὐδ' ὁ παυσάμενος τοῦ κατ' αὐτὴν ἐνεργεῖν. Ὅτι δὲ ὁ θεὸς δίκαιος, φησὶ Μωϋσῆς· “ὅσιος καὶ δίκαιος ὁ κύριος”· οὗτος πατὴρ τοῦ σωτῆρός ἐστι· “πάτερ δίκαιε, καὶ ὁ κόσμος σε οὐκ ἔγνω”· τούτου υἱὸς ὢν ὡς θεὸς ἐκ θεοῦ καὶ ἅγιος ἐξ ἁγίου, οὕτω καὶ δίκαιος ἐκ δικαίου ὑπάρχει· οὐ μάχεται τούτοις τὸ δικαιοσύνην αὐτὸν εἶναι λέγεσθαι· τὸ γὰρ κατ' οὐσίαν τοιοῦτον ῥηθείη δικαιοσύνη καὶ δίκαιος. (Cr 120, 30-121, 11 Ma 221) 52 νῦν τέκνα θεοῦ ἐσμεν τουτέστι κατὰ τὴν παροῦσαν ζωήν. (Ma 221) 57 Τοῦ Χρυσοστόμου. Ἐπείπερ πρὸ πάντων τραπεὶς ὁ διάβολος ἐν τῷ ἁμαρτάνειν γέγονεν, ἐξ αὐτοῦ χρηματίζει πᾶς ὁ ἁμαρτητικῶς ἐνεργῶν· προάρχεται γὰρ ἐν τῷ ἁμαρτάνοντι δι' ὑποβολὴν πονηρῶν λογισμῶν ὡς ἐπὶ τοῦ Ἰούδα. (Cr 123, 29-32 Ma 221) Ἀλλ' ἐρεῖ τις, ὅτι γίνεται ὁ διάβολος ἐν τοῖς ἁμαρτάνουσι τῶν πρὸ αὐτοῦ ἡμαρτηκότων ἐν τῷ διδόναι αὐτῷ τόπον· πρὸς ὃ λεκτέον ταὐτὸν εἶναι τὸ ποιεῖν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν τῷ ἁμαρτάνειν ἐν τῷ διδόναι τόπον τῷ διαβόλῳ· δίδωσι γὰρ 58 6 αὐτῷ τόπον ἐπιθυμίᾳ ὑπαχθεὶς μετὰ τὸ δέξασθαι αὐτὸν πρακτικῶς ἐπιτελῶν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν· τοῦτο γὰρ σημαίνει τὸ ποιεῖν αὐτήν· εὖ δὲ καὶ τὸ εἰπεῖν “ποιῶν”, ἀλλ' οὐ ποιήσας τοῦ μετανοήσαντος οὐκέτι ὄντος ἐκ τοῦ διαβόλου, ἀλλὰ μόνου τοῦ ἐνεργοῦντος αὐτὴν ἔτι· οὕτω γὰρ καὶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας δοῦλός ἐστιν ὁ ποιῶν, ἀλλ' οὐχ ὁ ποιήσας αὐτήν· “πᾶς γὰρ ὁ ποιῶν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν”, φησί, “δοῦλος αὐτῆς ἐστιν”. (Cr 123, 32-124, 10 Ma 222) 59 Σευήρου· καὶ τὴν αἰτίαν προστίθησι τοῦ μὴ δύνασθαι ἁμαρτάνειν λέγων, ὅτι σπέρμα αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ μένει· τί δέ ἐστι τὸ σπέρμα τοῦ θεοῦ τὸ μένον ἐπὶ τοὺς πιστούς; ἢ ἡ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἐπιφοίτησις, δι' ἧς ἀνεγεννήθημεν, 60 ἥτις οὐκ ἀφίσταται ἡμῶν, ὅταν κατὰ Παῦλον μὴ λυπῶμεν διὰ τῶν αἰσχίστων πράξεων τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τοῦ θεοῦ, ἐν ᾧ ἐσφραγίσθημεν εἰς ἡμέραν ἀποκαλύψεως. (Cr 124, 15-21 Ma 222) Καὶ γὰρ λέγοντες μὴ δύνασθαι ἀδικεῖν τὸν δικαιοσύνην ἔχοντα οὐκ ἀδυναμίαν φυσικὴν δηλοῦμεν, καθ' ἣν λέγομεν μὴ δύνασθαι τὸ ἄλογον ζῷον ἐπιστήμην ἢ ἕτερόν τι τοιοῦτον ἔχειν. (Cr 126, 25-28 Ma 222) Εἰ πᾶς ὁ ποιῶν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἐκ τοῦ διαβόλου ἐστίν, ἐκ τοῦ οὕτω πράττειν φανεροῦται ὢν τέκνον τοῦ διαβόλου, καθάπερ καὶ Ἐλύμας ὁ μάγος ἐκ τοῦ “πλήρης παντὸς δόλου” ἐγνώσθη υἱὸς διαβόλου· καὶ ἐπεὶ πᾶς ὁ γεγεννημένος ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ ἁμαρτίαν οὐ ποιεῖ τῷ ἔχειν ἐν ἑαυτῷ θεοῦ σπέρμα, τὸν οὕτω μὴ ἁμαρτάνοντα εὑρεῖν ἐστι σαφῶς υἱὸν ὄντα θεοῦ· προσέθηκα δὲ τῷ ἁμαρτάνοντι οὕτως, ἵνα μήτις σοφίσηται λέγων τέκνα θεοῦ ἡμᾶς τίθεσθαι πάντας τοὺς μὴ ἁμαρτάνοντας· τὰ γὰρ βρέφη ἁμαρτίαν μὴ ποιοῦντα οὐ ῥητέον τέκνα θεοῦ εἶναι· ἐξ ἡλικίας γάρ, ἀλλ' οὐκ ἐξ ἀρετῆς κωλύονται τοῦ ἁμαρτάνειν, ἵνα μὴ ἕτερόν τι εἴπωμεν φάσκοντες μὴ 61 ὑγιῶς λέγεσθαι περὶ βρεφῶν, ὅτι ἁμαρτίαν οὐ ποιοῦσιν· οὐ ταὐτὸν γὰρ τὸ μὴ ἁμαρτάνειν τῷ μὴ ποιεῖν ἁμαρτίαν· τὸ μὲν γὰρ ἀπόφασις ἔοικε, τὸ δὲ ἐκ διαθέσεως ὑπάρχει. (Cr 126, 13-25 Ma 222) Ἐπεὶ ὁ ποιῶν τὴν δικαιοσύνην ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ γεγέννηται, ἕπεται δὲ τῷ οὕτω γεννηθέντι ἀγαπᾶν τοὺς ἀδελφούς· ὁ μὴ ἔχων δικαιοσύνην τῷ μὴ ποιεῖν αὐτήν, μισῶν δὲ τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐκ ἔστιν· οὐ κατ' ἄλλον τρόπον ἢ τὸ μὴ γεγεννῆσθαι ἐξ αὐτοῦ· οὐ γὰρ προσεκτέον τοῖς λέγουσι μὴ εἶναι ἐκ θεοῦ τούτους διὰ χοϊκὴν φύσιν (Cr 127, 14-19) 62 Κόσμον γὰρ ἐνταῦθα τοὺς πονηροὺς ἀνθρώπους φησίν. (Cr 132, 13 Ma 225) 63 Ὅνπερ γὰρ τρόπον πρὸ τῆς Χριστοῦ παρουσίας ὄντων ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ θεοῦ προφητῶν πολλοὶ ἐτύγχανον ὑποκρινόμενοι τὴν προφητείαν ὡς χρείαν εἶναι ἐπιστήμης ἐξεταστικῆς, τίνες τῶν λεγόντων “τάδε λέγει κύριος” πνεῦμα ἅγιον καὶ θεοῦ λόγον εἶχον καὶ τίνες ὑπὸ πονηροῦ πνεύματος κινούμενοι τοῦ ψευδοῦς ἦσαν προφῆται, οὕτω καὶ μετὰ τὴν ἐπιδημίαν τῶν ἀποστόλων ἐν Χριστῷ λαλούντων καὶ
pass_a_gloss: [...] of all which (things) the one who disdains (looks down on) will be above the world, doing [fragment number 49] the wills of God by always abiding and loving God. [locator: Cr 116, 16-23, Ma 218] He says this since, having become disciples, they stood away from the truth, and invented blasphemies of their own devising. [Cr 118, 27-28] [50] The one who has grasped with knowledge (scientifically) about God, that he is righteous according to essence, will immediately have knowledge that the one doing his righteousness is begotten from him; just as the one who knew him being holiness gives himself up to being sanctified, understanding [51] exactly the (saying): 'You shall be holy, because I am holy'; and well also (is) the saying 'doing', but not 'having done' or 'going to do' righteousness; virtue, being practical, presents the one who exercises (it) as righteous; so no one before doing it is righteous, nor the one who has stopped acting according to it. And that God is righteous, Moses says: 'holy and righteous (is) the Lord'; this one is father of the Savior: 'righteous Father, and the world did not know you'; being son of this one as God from God and holy from holy, so also he is righteous from righteous; it does not fight against these (things) that he is said to be righteousness; for what is such according to essence may be called righteousness and righteous. [Cr 120, 30-121, 11, Ma 221] [52] 'Now we are children of God', that is, according to the present life. [Ma 221] [57] Of Chrysostom. Since before all, having turned, the devil came to be in sinning, from him is styled everyone who acts sinfully; for he takes the lead in the one sinning through suggestion of evil thoughts, as in the case of Judas. [Cr 123, 29-32, Ma 221] But someone will say that the devil comes to be in those sinning, of those who have sinned before him, by giving him place; to which it must be said that doing the sin is the same as sinning by giving place to the devil; for he gives [58, 6] him place, being led on by desire, after receiving him, accomplishing the sin practically; for this signifies 'doing' it; and well also the saying 'doing', but not 'having done', the one who has repented no longer being from the devil, but only the one still working it; for so also the one doing (it) is slave of sin, but not the one who has done it: 'for everyone doing the sin', he says, 'is its slave'. [Cr 123, 32-124, 10, Ma 222] [59] Of Severus: and he adds the cause of not being able to sin, saying that his seed abides in him; and what is the seed of God abiding upon the faithful? Or (is it not) the visitation (coming upon) of the Holy Spirit, through which we were born again, [60] which does not stand away from us, whenever, according to Paul, we do not grieve through the most shameful deeds the Holy Spirit of God, in whom we were sealed for the day of revelation. [Cr 124, 15-21, Ma 222] For indeed, saying that the one having righteousness is not able to do wrong, we do not show a natural inability, according to which we say that the irrational animal is not able to have knowledge or some other such thing. [Cr 126, 25-28, Ma 222] If everyone doing the sin is from the devil, from acting so he is made manifest being a child of the devil, just as Elymas the magician also from the 'full of all deceit' was known as son of the devil; and since everyone who has been begotten from God does not do sin by having in himself God's seed, it is possible to find the one thus not sinning clearly being a son of God; and I added 'thus' to the 'sinning', so that no one may sophisticate saying that we set as children of God all those not sinning; for the infants, not doing sin, are not to be said to be children of God; for from age, but not from virtue, they are hindered from sinning, so that we do not say something else, asserting that [61] it is not soundly said about infants that they do not do sin; for not sinning is not the same as not doing sin; for the one resembles a negation, but the other exists from disposition. [Cr 126, 13-25, Ma 222] Since the one doing the righteousness has been begotten from God, and it follows for the one thus begotten to love the brothers; the one not having righteousness by not doing it, and hating his brother, is not from God; not in another way than not having been begotten from him; for one must not pay heed to those saying that these are not from God because of an earthy (dust-made) nature [Cr 127, 14-19] [62] For he here says 'world' (meaning) the wicked men. [Cr 132, 13, Ma 225] [63] For in the very way that before the presence of Christ, there being prophets of God in Judea, many happened to be feigning prophecy, so that there was need of an examining knowledge (to tell) which of those saying 'thus says the Lord' had Holy Spirit and God's word, and which, being moved by an evil spirit, were prophets of the false; so also after the arrival of the apostles speaking in Christ and [continues: having the Holy Spirit ...].
pass_b_english: …Whoever looks down on all these things will be above the world, doing the will of God by abiding forever and loving God (1 John 2:17).
He says this because, after becoming disciples, they departed from the truth (1 John 2:19) and invented blasphemies of their own devising.

Whoever has understood with true knowledge that God is righteous in his very being will at once know that the one who does his righteousness is born of him (1 John 2:29); just as the one who knows that he is holiness gives himself over to being made holy, since he understands exactly the saying, "You shall be holy, for I am holy" (1 Peter 1:16). It is well said, too, that he "does" righteousness, not that he "did" or "will do" it. Virtue, being a thing of practice, makes the one who exercises it righteous; so no one is righteous before he does it, nor is the one who has stopped acting by it. That God is righteous, Moses says: "Holy and righteous is the Lord" (Deuteronomy 32:4). He is the Father of the Savior: "Righteous Father, the world has not known you" (John 17:25). Being his Son, as God from God and holy from holy, he is likewise righteous from righteous. It is no contradiction that he is also said to be righteousness; for what is such in its very being may be called both righteousness and righteous.
"Now we are children of God" (1 John 3:2): that is, in the present life.

From Chrysostom: Since the devil turned away before anyone else and came to be in sin, everyone who acts sinfully is named as being of him. For he takes the lead in the one who sins by suggesting evil thoughts, as in the case of Judas.

But someone will say that the devil comes to be in sinners who had already sinned before him, by their giving him place. To this we must answer that doing sin is the same thing as sinning by giving place to the devil. For a man gives him place when, led on by desire, after receiving him, he carries out the sin in action; that is what "doing" it means. It is well said, too, that he "does" and not that he "did": the one who has repented is no longer of the devil, but only the one who is still committing it. So too it is the one who does sin, not the one who did it, who is the slave of sin: "For everyone who does sin," he says, "is its slave" (John 8:34).

From Severus: He also adds the reason why such a man cannot sin, saying that "his seed remains in him." What is the seed of God that remains upon the faithful? Is it not the coming of the Holy Spirit, through which we were born again? It does not leave us, so long as, in Paul's words, we do not grieve by shameful deeds the Holy Spirit of God, in whom we were sealed for the day of revelation.

For when we say that one who has righteousness cannot do wrong, we do not mean a natural inability, the kind by which we say that an irrational animal cannot have knowledge or anything else of that sort.

If everyone who does sin is of the devil (1 John 3:8), then by acting so he is shown to be a child of the devil, just as Elymas the magician was known to be a son of the devil from his being "full of all deceit" (Acts 13:10). And since everyone who has been born of God does not do sin, because he has the seed of God in himself (1 John 3:9), the one who does not sin in this way can clearly be found to be a son of God. I added "in this way" to "not sinning" so that no one may quibble and say that we count all who do not sin as children of God. Infants, for example, who do not do sin, are not to be called children of God: it is their age, not virtue, that keeps them from sinning. And that is without adding a further point, that it is not even sound to say of infants that they do not do sin. For not sinning is not the same as not doing sin: the one seems to be a bare negation, while the other comes from a settled disposition.

Since the one who does righteousness has been born of God, and loving the brothers follows for one so born, the one who does not have righteousness, because he does not do it, and who hates his brother, is not of God (1 John 3:10), in no other sense than that he has not been born of him. For no heed should be paid to those who say that such people are not of God because of an earthly nature.
For by "the world" here he means wicked people (1 John 3:13).

For in the same way as before the coming of Christ, when there were prophets of God in Judea, many happened to be feigning prophecy, so that a searching skill was needed to tell which of those who said "Thus says the Lord" had the Holy Spirit and the word of God, and which were prophets of falsehood, moved by an evil spirit (1 John 4:1); so also after the arrival of the apostles, who spoke in Christ and …

lemmas.gloss: in essence, in his very being

choices.term: ὅταν κατὰ Παῦλον μὴ λυπῶμεν ... τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον
choices.english: so long as, in Paul's words, we do not grieve ... the Holy Spirit of God
choices.why: μή negates λυπῶμεν: the Spirit stays while we do NOT grieve him. The old English dropped the negation ('which is not taken from us when ... we grieve the Holy Spirit').
rejected: which is not taken from us when ... we grieve the Holy Spirit of God

choices.term: τὸ μὲν γὰρ ἀπόφασις ἔοικε, τὸ δὲ ἐκ διαθέσεως ὑπάρχει
choices.english: the one seems to be a bare negation, while the other comes from a settled disposition
choices.why: ἀπόφασις is 'negation', not 'decision'; the old English had 'a matter of decision'.
χοϊκός, of dust (1 Corinthians 15:47); the old English had 'a corrupt nature'.
Catena headings rendered as lead-ins, as for catena tags in the round-1 works; the old English turned Severus's heading into 'They say'.

choices.english: who had already sinned before him
choices.why: αὐτοῦ is the devil; the objection appears to put the sinning before the devil's entry. Kept close to the Greek and noted.
